overview: White strikes in the centre at once with 3.d4. After 3...exd4 White either plays 4.e5 d5 5.Bb5+ (the Urusov Gambit) or 4.Nf3 Nxe4 5.Qxd4, giving a pawn for rapid development and open lines against the black king. Black can keep the pawn if he finds the right defensive moves; White gets lines and tempi in return. Positions are open and tactical.

white_ideas.idea: Give a pawn for development and open lines, with Bb5+, Nf3 and Bg5 or Qxd4.
Use the c4 bishop and the d-file to harass the black king before it castles.

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawn on d4, then ...d5 or ...Nxe4 and complete development.
Neutralise the initiative, castle, and rely on the extra pawn.

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after ...exd4 with White ahead in development and Black a pawn up.
After 4.e5 d5 5.Bb5+ the e5 pawn cramps Black while the c8 bishop and knights get active squares.

character.notes: A gambit with early central tension, forcing piece play and attacking chances for White. Both sides take risks.

gambit.notes: After 3...exd4 White has no immediate way to regain d4; Black can keep the extra pawn (4.Nf3 Nxe4 5.Qxd4 Nf6).

soundness.notes: Believed to be acceptable but not best; Black gets adequate counterplay with accurate play. Consider it close to equal at club level, a bit risky at top level.

structure.notes: Open centre with d-file and diagonals for the pieces.

approach.notes: Very rare among strong players; mostly played for surprise. 3.d3 and 3.Nc3 are the normal moves.

level.notes: A sharp gambit whose follow-ups need to be learned; not a good first choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Urusov Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nf6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nf3
sublines_that_differ.how: White pins the e4 knight tactics with Qxd4 after ...Nxe4; very similar to the Ponziani-Urusov structures.

sublines_that_differ.name: Declined 3...Nxe4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nf6 3. d4 Nxe4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black grabs the e-pawn and 4.dxe5 is a different, quieter game.

character.reason: Early central break, gambit, open lines and attacking chances.

gambit.reason: White gives a pawn for development that Black can keep.

soundness.reason: Black has several adequate defences and White gets real activity, though risky.

structure.reason: The centre opens straight away after ...exd4.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose 3.d4 here; it is mostly a surprise weapon.

level.reason: Gambit needs memorised sharp lines, but ideas are clear for the player with White.

plans.reason: Material is sacrificed for tempo and attacking lines against f7.
